kira: Heads-up — after yesterday's packer change I see a 12-18% p95 latency regression on small-batch INT8 weight-only workloads (AWQ path). Seen on dedicated infra in us-west1. :eyes:
aj: ugh. did you run a perf profile? is this kernel selection or packing overhead?
mateo: I pulled a brief perf trace, attaching top lines. looks like unpack+repack in hotpath and KV cache miss spikes around the same time.
mateo: ```
# perf top snapshot (sampled)
  18.3% pack_kernel_unpack
  12.1% runtime_dispatcher
  9.7% kv_cache_lookup
  5.4% awq_matmul_int8
  4.8% memcpy
```
kira: thanks. pattern: group_size=32 experiments show lower throughput than group_size=16 for this workload — packing CPU cost dominates when sequence_len < 64 and batch_size <= 4.
perf-bot: perf-alert: p95_latency_up 15% for model-opt-int8-awq in us-west1 (detected 2025-10-04T14:05:12Z)
sasha: Are we sure it's AWQ vs GPTQ? GPTQ path uses different packing stride, right?
mateo: good point — I compared AWQ vs GPTQ on same bin and AWQ shows higher unpack calls because we cache at group granularity differently. GPTQ pre-packs into contiguous buffers so less memcpy.
aj: so root cause sounds like packing/unpacking CPU work + KV thrash due to group-aligned cache misses. two levers: 1) avoid unpack for tiny groups, 2) change kernel selector to prefer kernels that operate on packed layout in-place for small seqs.
kira: I tried a quick patch to short-circuit packer when batch_size*seq_len < 256 — avoids doing pack/unpack and routes to in-place kernel. microbench: p95 down ~9% but throughput slightly worse for big batches.
sasha: can we do adaptive heuristic? if batch_size<=4 && seq_len<=64 && group_size>=32 then skip pack. store as flag in trace.
mateo: also observed KV cache eviction rate spikes when we increase group_size to 64 — because packed buffers are larger and we blow the kvcache budget more often. That explains latency tail.
aj: telemetry idea: emit pack_bytes and kvcache_evictions per request. add to token-level metrics so Optimize can reason about unit cost.
perf-bot: note: rollback candidate flagged for packer change PR #4123 — revert suggested if cannot ship fallback quickly.
kira: plan: 1) add adaptive skip-pack heuristic behind runtime flag (kira/skip_pack_small) 2) add kernel selector rule to prefer in-place kernels for small seqs 3) emit pack_bytes + kv_evictions in console 4) run canary on dedicated in us-west1 w/ traffic split 5%->25% over 2h.
sasha: I'll own the canary config. aj can you review kernel selector rule? mateo please add metric emission.
aj: on it. quick note: also double-check quant calibration side effects — AWQ calibration changes per-group scales and can increase compute in prolog. but perf traces show pack/unpack is dominant here.
mateo: one more data point — ran AWQ vs GPTQ end-to-end with same group_size=32, skip-pack patch applied. AWQ p95 -> 6% better, GPTQ ~2% better. so still AWQ slightly worse but close.
kira: thanks team. I'll open a short-lived feature flag PR and link it here. if rollback gets noisy we revert packer change. :+1:
